resposta:
**Secretários de Energia dos Estados Unidos (início de 2018 – fim de 2024)**  
*(incluindo secretários interinos)*  

| Nome | Partido | Início | Fim | Observações |
|------|---------|--------|-----|-------------|
| **Rick Perry** | República Republicana | 2 de março de 2017 | 1 de dez de 2019 | Governou durante todo o período de 2018. Renunciou em 17 de outubro de 2019. |
| **Dan Brouillette** | República Republicana | 1 de dez de 2019* | 20 de janeiro de 2021 | Confirmado pelo Senado em 2 de dez de 2019; assumiu como secretário interino após a saída de Perry. Serviu até a nomeação de Jennifer Granholm. |
| **David G. Huizenga** | Partido Democrata | 20 de janeiro de 2021 | 25 de fevereiro de 2021 | Interino nomeado para assumir enquanto Granholm era senador. Serviu apenas por cerca de duas semanas. |
| **Jennifer Granholm** | Partido Democrata | 25 de fevereiro de 2021 | 20 de janeiro de 2025 | Eleita 16ª Secretária de Energia em 2021 e permaneceu até 20 de janeiro de 2025. |

\* *Data exato de tomada de posse:* 11 de dez de 2019 (após confirmação do Senado).  
\*\* *Período de secretário interino:* começa com a confirmação e continua até a aprovação pela Câmara e Senado.

### Resumo cronológico (2018‑2024)

1. **2018** – Rick Perry (Rep.) governa desde março de 2017 até dezembro de 2019.  
2. **Novembro – dezembro 2019** – Dan Brouillette é confirmado e assume como secretário interino (efeito imediato após a renúncia de Perry).  
3. **Janeiro 2021** – David Huizenga (D) atua como secretário interino para aguardar a confirmação de Jennifer Granholm.  
4. **Fevereiro 2021** – Jennifer Granholm toma posse e governa até 20 de janeiro de 2025.

> **Nota:** A partir de 3 de fevereiro de 2025, Chris Wright assume a nova missão (fora do intervalo solicitado), mas isso ocorre depois do fim de 2024.

---

**Fontes utilizadas**

- Rick Perry – [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry) (in office: 2017‑2019)  
- Dan Brouillette – [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette) (in office: 2019‑2021)  
- David Huizenga – [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Huizenga) (acting secretary: 2021)  
- Jennifer Granholm – [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Granholm) (in office: 2021‑2025)

The **United States secretary of energy** is the head of the [United States Department of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Energy "United States Department of Energy"), a member of the [Cabinet of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States") and fifteenth in the [presidential line of succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_line_of_succession "United States presidential line of succession"). The position was created on October 1, 1977, when President [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter") signed the [Department of Energy Organization Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Energy_Organization_Act "Department of Energy Organization Act"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-2) establishing the department. Originally, the secretary and the department focused on energy production and regulation. Over time, the emphasis shifted to developing technology for more efficient energy sources and energy education. After the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), the department's attention also turned to [radioactive waste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_waste "Radioactive waste") disposal and environmental quality maintenance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-3)

Former [secretary of defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense "United States Secretary of Defense") [James Schlesinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_R._Schlesinger "James R. Schlesinger") was the first secretary of energy. As a Republican nominated by Democratic president Jimmy Carter, Schlesinger’s appointment remains the only instance of a president choosing a member of another political party for the position. Schlesinger is also the only secretary to be dismissed from the post.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-4) [Hazel O'Leary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazel_R._O'Leary "Hazel R. O'Leary"), [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton")’s first secretary of energy, was the first female and first African American to hold the position.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-5) The first [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") to serve as energy secretary was Clinton’s second energy secretary, [Federico Peña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Peña "Federico Peña"). [Spencer Abraham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spencer_Abraham "Spencer Abraham") became the first [Arab American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Americans "Arab Americans") to hold the position on January 20, 2001, under President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush"). [Steven Chu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Chu "Steven Chu"), appointed on January 20, 2009, under President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"), became the first [Asian American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans "Asian Americans") to hold the position. Chu also served as the longest-serving secretary of energy and was the first individual to join the Cabinet after having received a Nobel Prize.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-6) Former Michigan governor, [Jennifer Granholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Granholm "Jennifer Granholm"), confirmed on February 25, 2021 under President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden"), was the second woman to lead the Department of Energy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-7) [Chris Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Wright "Chris Wright") is the current secretary of energy under the Trump administration, confirmed on February, 3, 2025.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-8)

## Nuclear weapons

In addition to responsibilities related to generation and use of energy, the secretary is the most senior official other than the president of the United States or secretary of defense with primary responsibility for the nation's approximately 3,800 viable nuclear weapons. This arrangement is intended to maintain full civilian control over strategic weapons, except as directed by the president for specific military uses.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-9) The department of energy is responsible for the building, maintenance, and disposal of all nuclear weapons within the United States' arsenal in addition to safeguarding these weapons when they are not actively deployed in military service.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-10) Under the terms of several successive treaties, most recently New START, the United States has reduced its strategic arsenal to 1,500 deployed weapons. Consequently, many older legacy weapons systems have been dismantled or scheduled for dismantlement, with their core radioactive fuel - generally plutonium - being reprocessed into reactor-grade or space exploration fuel.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy#cite_note-11)

**James Richard Perry** (born March 4, 1950) is an American politician who served as the 14th [United States secretary of energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Secretary of Energy") from 2017 to 2019. He previously served as the 47th [governor of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Texas "Governor of Texas") from 2000 to 2015 and ran unsuccessfully for the [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") nomination for [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") in the [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries "2012 Republican Party presidential primaries") and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries "2016 Republican Party presidential primaries") elections.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-4)

Born into a family of cotton farmers in [Haskell, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haskell,_Texas "Haskell, Texas"), Perry graduated from [Texas A&M University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_University "Texas A&M University") in 1972 and entered into the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force"), serving a five-year stint and achieving the rank of [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(United_States_O-3) "Captain (United States O-3)").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-auto3-5) After leaving the Air Force in 1977, Perry returned to Texas and entered politics, serving as a member of the [Texas House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_House_of_Representatives "Texas House of Representatives") from 1985 to 1991. Initially a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"), Perry switched parties in 1989 and became a [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), and was elected [Agriculture Commissioner of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Department_of_Agriculture "Texas Department of Agriculture") the following year. In 1998, Perry was elected [lieutenant governor of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_governor_of_Texas "Lieutenant governor of Texas"), becoming the state's first Republican lieutenant governor since [Reconstruction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconstruction_era "Reconstruction era").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-8)

Perry assumed the governorship of Texas in December 2000, after Governor [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") resigned following his [election as president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election "2000 United States presidential election"). Perry was elected governor in 2002 and was re-elected in 2006 and 2010, becoming the longest-serving governor in Texas history. As governor, Perry identified as a staunch [conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_conservatism "American conservatism"), enacting [conservative fiscal policies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiscal_conservatism "Fiscal conservatism"), [restrictions on abortion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Types_of_abortion_restrictions_in_the_United_States "Types of abortion restrictions in the United States") and expanded [gun rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_keep_and_bear_arms "Right to keep and bear arms").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-auto-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-auto2-10) Long considered a potential presidential candidate, Perry officially announced his candidacy for the [2012 Republican nomination for president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries "2012 Republican Party presidential primaries") in August 2011. Perry initially performed well in polling and showed strong fundraising prowess, leading to him being considered a serious contender for the nomination. However, his support declined following debates and early primaries, and he withdrew from the race in January 2012.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-nyt120119a-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-14)

Perry declined to seek re-election to a fourth term as governor and left office in 2015, launching a [second presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry_2016_presidential_campaign "Rick Perry 2016 presidential campaign") shortly thereafter. Perry's second presidential campaign failed to garner substantial polling support, fundraising or media attention, leading him to withdraw from the race after only three months.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-auto1-15) Perry was initially a vocal opponent of [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s [2016 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump_2016_presidential_campaign "Donald Trump 2016 presidential campaign"), however, he later endorsed Trump after he secured the Republican nomination.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-16) After [winning the presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election"), Trump appointed Perry as Secretary of Energy, and he was confirmed by the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") in a 62–37 vote on March 2, 2017. On October 17, 2019, Perry reported to Trump that he intended to resign at the end of the year. His departure came amid scrutiny of his involvement in the [Trump–Ukraine scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump–Ukraine_scandal "Trump–Ukraine scandal"), which subsequently led to Trump's impeachment. He left office on December 1, 2019.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-HillLastDay-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-20)

## Early life

A fifth-generation Texan, Perry was born on March 4, 1950, in [Haskell, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haskell,_Texas "Haskell, Texas"), and raised in [Paint Creek, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paint_Creek,_Texas "Paint Creek, Texas"), the son of dryland cotton farmers Joseph Ray Perry and Amelia June Holt Perry. He has one older sister. Perry's ancestry is almost entirely English, dating as far back as the original [Thirteen Colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteen_Colonies "Thirteen Colonies").[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] His family has been in Texas since before the [Texas Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Revolution "Texas Revolution").[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*][[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-26)

His father, a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"), was a long-time Haskell County commissioner and school board member. Perry has said that his interest in politics probably began in November 1961, when his father took him to the funeral of U.S. Representative [Sam Rayburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Rayburn "Sam Rayburn").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-29)

Perry was in the [Boy Scouts of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Scouts_of_America "Boy Scouts of America") (BSA) and earned the rank of [Eagle Scout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagle_Scout_(Boy_Scouts_of_America) "Eagle Scout (Boy Scouts of America)").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-bio-30) The BSA has honored Perry with the [Distinguished Eagle Scout Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distinguished_Eagle_Scout_Award "Distinguished Eagle Scout Award").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-PerryDESA-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-33)

### College

Perry attended [Texas A&M University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_University "Texas A&M University") where he was a member of the [Corps of Cadets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_University_Corps_of_Cadets "Texas A&M University Corps of Cadets") and the [Alpha Gamma Rho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_Gamma_Rho "Alpha Gamma Rho") fraternity. He was elected senior class social secretary, a member and [redpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggie_Bonfire_leadership "Aggie Bonfire leadership") in [Aggie Bonfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggie_Bonfire "Aggie Bonfire"), and one of A&M's five ["yell leaders"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggie_Yell_Leaders "Aggie Yell Leaders").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-time20090125-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-35) He graduated in 1972 with a Bachelor of Science degree in [animal science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_science "Animal science").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-aggiestime-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-39)

In 1989, he said, "I was probably a bit of a free spirit, not particularly structured real well for life outside of a military regime, I would have not lasted at [Texas Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Tech_University "Texas Tech University") or the [University of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas "University of Texas"). I would have hit the fraternity scene and lasted about one semester."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-aggiestime-36)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-40)

### First jobs

In the early 1970s, Perry interned during several summers with [Southwestern Advantage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_Advantage "Southwestern Advantage"), as a door-to-door book salesman. "I count my time working for Dortch Oldham [then president of the [Southwestern family of companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_family_of_companies "Southwestern family of companies")] as one of the most important formative experiences of my life", Perry said in 2010. "There is nothing that tests your commitment to a goal like getting a few doors closed in your face." He said that "Mr. Oldham taught legions of young people to communicate quickly, clearly and with passion, a lesson that has served me well in my life since then."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-42)

Upon graduation from college in 1972, Perry was commissioned as an officer in the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") and completed pilot training in February 1974. He was then assigned as a [Lockheed C-130 Hercules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_C-130_Hercules "Lockheed C-130 Hercules") pilot with the [772nd Tactical Airlift Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/772d_Expeditionary_Airlift_Squadron "772d Expeditionary Airlift Squadron") at [Dyess Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyess_Air_Force_Base "Dyess Air Force Base"), located in Abilene, Texas. Perry's duties included two-month overseas rotations at [RAF Mildenhall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAF_Mildenhall "RAF Mildenhall"), located in [Mildenhall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mildenhall,_Suffolk "Mildenhall, Suffolk"), England, and [Rhein-Main Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhein-Main_Air_Base "Rhein-Main Air Base"), located at Frankfurt am Main, Germany. His missions included a 1974 [U.S. State Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State") drought relief effort in [Mali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mali "Mali"), [Mauritania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritania "Mauritania") and [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad"), and, in 1976, earthquake relief in [Guatemala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala "Guatemala").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-43) He left the Air Force in 1977 at the rank of [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(United_States_O-3) "Captain (United States O-3)"), returned to Texas, and went into farming cotton with his father.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-auto3-5)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-45)

## Early political career

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Bush_Contact_Sheet_P17939_%28cropped2%29.jpg/250px-Bush_Contact_Sheet_P17939_%28cropped2%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bush_Contact_Sheet_P17939_(cropped2).jpg)Perry with President [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") in 1990

### Texas Legislature

In 1984, Perry was elected to the [Texas House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_House_of_Representatives "Texas House of Representatives") as a Democrat from district 64, which included his home county of [Haskell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haskell_County,_Texas "Haskell County, Texas"). He served on the House Appropriations and Calendars committees during his three two-year terms in office. He befriended fellow freshman state representative [Lena Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lena_Guerrero "Lena Guerrero"), a staunch liberal Democrat who endorsed Perry's reelection bid in 2006.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-48)

Perry was part of the "Pit Bulls", a group of Appropriations members who sat on the lower dais in the committee room ("the pit") who pushed for austere state budgets during the 1980s.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-49) At one point, *[The Dallas Morning News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dallas_Morning_News "The Dallas Morning News")* named him one of the ten most effective members of the legislature.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-52)

In 1987, Perry voted for a $5.7 billion tax increase proposed by Republican Governor [Bill Clements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clements "Bill Clements").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-53) Perry supported [Al Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore "Al Gore") in the 1988 Democratic presidential primaries and worked for Gore's campaign in Texas.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-poli_Rick-54) On September 29, 1989, Perry announced that he was switching parties, becoming a Republican.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-55) On a guest appearance on [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News "Fox News") show [Hannity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hannity "Sean Hannity"), he partially credits [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan") as part of the reason he became a Republican, also stating he switched political parties sooner in his life than Reagan.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-59)

### Agriculture Commissioner

In 1990, as a newly minted Republican, Perry challenged [Jim Hightower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Hightower "Jim Hightower"), the incumbent Democratic [Agriculture Commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Agriculture_Commissioner "Texas Agriculture Commissioner"). [Karl Rove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Rove "Karl Rove") was Perry's campaign manager.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-62)

In the Republican primary on March 13, 1990, Perry polled 276,558 votes (47%), with [Richard McIver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_McIver "Richard McIver") garnering 176,976 votes (30%) and Gene L. Duke, who placed third, polling 132,497 votes (23%).[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-63) Since Perry fell shy of the necessary 50% to win outright, a runoff was held between Perry and McIver set on April 10, 1990. In the runoff, he emerged victorious, garnering 96,649 votes (69%) to McIver's 43,921 votes (31%).[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-64) [[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-65) During 1990, Hightower's office was embroiled in an FBI investigation into corruption and bribery. Three aides were convicted in 1993 of using public funds for political fundraising, although Hightower himself was not found to be involved in the wrongdoings.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-66) Perry narrowly defeated Hightower in November 1990, garnering 1,864,463 votes (49%) to Hightower's 1,820,145 votes (48%).[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-68) [[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-70) Rove raised $3 million to raise Perry's profile, "while tarnishing the name of Jim Hightower" resulting in Perry's name becoming a "household name in Texas—and Hightower's name synonymous with corruption".[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-71) [[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-72) As Agriculture Commissioner, Perry was responsible for promoting the sale of Texas farm produce to other states and foreign nations, and for supervising the calibration of weights and measures, such as [gasoline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasoline "Gasoline") pumps and [grocery store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grocery_store "Grocery store") scales.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-75)

In April 1993, Perry, while serving as Texas agriculture commissioner, expressed support for the effort [to reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care_reform_in_the_United_States "Health care reform in the United States") the nation's healthcare, describing it as "most commendable".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-76) The healthcare plan, first revealed in September, was ultimately [unsuccessful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_health_care_plan_of_1993#Defeat "Clinton health care plan of 1993") due to Republican congressional opposition.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-81) In 2005, after being questioned on the issue by a potential opponent in the Republican governor primary, Perry said he expressed his support only in order to get [the Clintons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_family "Clinton family") to pay more attention to rural healthcare.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-84)

In 1994, Perry was reelected Agriculture Commissioner by a large margin, getting 2,546,287 votes (62 percent) to Democrat Marvin Gregory's 1,479,692 (36 percent). [Libertarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States) "Libertarian Party (United States)") Clyde L. Garland received the remaining 85,836 votes (2 percent).[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-1994_General_Election-85) Gregory, a chicken farmer from [Sulphur Springs, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulphur_Springs,_Texas "Sulphur Springs, Texas"), was on the Texas Agricultural Finance Authority with Perry in the early '90s as a Republican but became a Democrat before running against Perry in 1994.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-88)

### Lieutenant governor

In 1998, Perry ran for [lieutenant governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_Texas "Lieutenant Governor of Texas"). During this election, Perry had a notable falling out with his previous top political strategist Karl Rove, which began the much-reported rivalry between the [Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") and Perry camps.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-89) Perry polled 1,858,837 votes (50.05 percent) to the 1,790,106 (48.20 percent) cast for Democrat [John Sharp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sharp_(Texas_politician) "John Sharp (Texas politician)"). Perry became the state's [first Republican lieutenant governor since Reconstruction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_Texas#Lieutenant_governors_of_Texas "Lieutenant Governor of Texas"), taking office on January 19, 1999.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-92)

## Governor of Texas

Main article: [Governorship of Rick Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governorship_of_Rick_Perry "Governorship of Rick Perry")

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/FEMA_-_16240_-_Photograph_by_Ed_Edahl_taken_on_09-27-2005_in_Texas.jpg/250px-FEMA_-_16240_-_Photograph_by_Ed_Edahl_taken_on_09-27-2005_in_Texas.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FEMA_-_16240_-_Photograph_by_Ed_Edahl_taken_on_09-27-2005_in_Texas.jpg)President George W. Bush and Texas Governor Rick Perry shake hands September 27, 2005, after a question-and-answer session at the Port Arthur airport. Port Arthur suffered extensive damage from [Hurricane Rita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Rita "Hurricane Rita").

Perry assumed the office of governor on December 21, 2000, following the resignation of [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush")—who was preparing to become [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-bio-30) He won the office in his own right in the [2002 gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_gubernatorial_election,_2002 "Texas gubernatorial election, 2002"), where he received 58% of votes to Laredo oilman and businessman [Tony Sanchez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Sanchez_(politician) "Tony Sanchez (politician)")'s 40%.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-1994_General_Election-85) He was re-elected in the [2006 gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_gubernatorial_election,_2006 "Texas gubernatorial election, 2006") against three major opponents, polling 39% of votes against runner-up former U.S. Congressman [Chris Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Bell_(politician) "Chris Bell (politician)") of Houston with 30%. Former Republican Comptroller, [Carole Keeton Strayhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carole_Keeton_Strayhorn "Carole Keeton Strayhorn"), running as an independent, garnered 18% of the vote and comic/author/musician, [Kinky Friedman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinky_Friedman "Kinky Friedman"), also running as an independent, garnered over 12%. In the [2010 gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_gubernatorial_election,_2010 "Texas gubernatorial election, 2010"), Perry became the first Texas governor to be elected to three four-year terms, polling 55% of votes to former Houston Mayor [Bill White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_White_(Texas_politician) "Bill White (Texas politician)")'s 42%.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-96)

In the 2001 legislative session, Perry set a record for his use of the [veto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veto "Veto"), rejecting 82 acts, more than any other governor in any single legislative session in the history of the state since [Reconstruction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconstruction_era_of_the_United_States "Reconstruction era of the United States").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Vetoes-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Vetoes_2-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-100)

Perry is one of five governors of Texas to have served three terms, the others being [Allan Shivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allan_Shivers "Allan Shivers"), [Price Daniel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Price_Daniel "Price Daniel"), [John Connally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Connally "John Connally") and later [Greg Abbott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Abbott "Greg Abbott"). He is the longest-serving governor in Texas history. He had served for 14 years by the time he left office, making him the second longest-serving U.S. governor at the time, behind [Terry Branstad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Branstad "Terry Branstad") of Iowa.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-102)

### Fiscal policies

In his presidential campaign, Perry highlighted the economic success Texas achieved under his governorship. The efficacy of Perry's economic policies has been questioned by some sources, including [Ezra Klein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Klein "Ezra Klein").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-107)

A proclaimed proponent of fiscal conservatism, Perry often campaigned on job growth and tax issues, such as his opposition to creating a state [income tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_tax "Income tax"). In 2002, Perry refused to promise not to raise taxes as governor, and in the following years did propose or approve various tax and debt increases.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-perrytaxes-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-109)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-auto-9)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-110) In 2009, Perry signed [Grover Norquist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grover_Norquist "Grover Norquist")'s pledge to "oppose and veto any and all efforts to increase taxes".[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-113)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-114)

Texas began borrowing money in 2003 to pay for roads and was projected to owe $17.3 billion by the end of 2012, increasing total state debt from $13.4 billion in 2001 to $37.8 billion in 2011.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-115) The state's public finance authority sold $2 billion in bonds for unemployment benefits, and it was authorized to sell $1.5 billion more if necessary. Texas federal borrowing topped $1.6 billion in October 2010, before the bond sales.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-117)

In 2003, Perry signed legislation that created the [Texas Enterprise Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Enterprise_Fund "Texas Enterprise Fund"), which has since given $435 million in grants to businesses. *The New York Times* reported that many of the companies receiving grants, or their chief executives, have made contributions to Perry's campaigns or to the Republican Governors Association.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Confessore-118) (Perry became chairman of the group in 2008 and again in 2011.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-rga.org-119)) Perry was criticized for supporting corporate tax breaks and other incentives, while the state government was experiencing budget deficits.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-121)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-123)

### Healthcare

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Texas_Governor_Rick_Perry_speaking_at_the_Houston_Technology_Center_in_2010.jpg/250px-Texas_Governor_Rick_Perry_speaking_at_the_Houston_Technology_Center_in_2010.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Texas_Governor_Rick_Perry_speaking_at_the_Houston_Technology_Center_in_2010.jpg)Perry speaking at the [Houston Technology Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Technology_Center "Houston Technology Center") in 2010

As governor, Perry was an opponent of federal health-care reform proposals and of the [Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patient_Protection_and_Affordable_Care_Act "Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act"), describing the latter as "socialism on American soil".[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-nyt-healthcare-124) His focus in Texas was on [tort reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tort_reform "Tort reform"), signing a bill in 2003 that restricted non-economic damages in [medical malpractice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_malpractice "Medical malpractice") judgments.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-125) Perry touted this approach in his presidential campaign, although independent analysts have concluded that it has failed to increase the supply of physicians or limit health-care costs in Texas. A separate 2013 study, however, reported increased physician growth after the 2003 reforms.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-nyt-healthcare-124)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-cost-curve-126)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-127)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-128)

During Perry's governorship, Texas rose from second to first among states with the highest proportion of uninsured residents at 26%, and had the lowest level of access to [prenatal care in the U.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prenatal_care_in_the_United_States "Prenatal care in the United States") Perry and the state legislature cut [Medicaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicaid "Medicaid") spending.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-nyt-healthcare-124)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-la-times-healthcare-129) The *[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")* wrote that under Perry, "working Texans increasingly have been priced out of private healthcare while the state's safety net has withered."[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-la-times-healthcare-129)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-130)

Perry's office said that Texas represents a model private-sector approach to healthcare. His spokeswoman said, "Texas does provide an adequate safety net to those truly in need... and many individuals simply choose not to purchase healthcare coverage."[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-la-times-healthcare-129)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-131)

In December 2011, Perry said he had undergone a "transformation" and now opposed abortions, even in cases of rape and incest. The next day he clarified that he would allow an exception for abortions that would save a mother's life.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-132)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-134)

In February 2007, Perry issued an [executive order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_order_(United_States) "Executive order (United States)") mandating that Texas girls receive the [HPV vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HPV_vaccine "HPV vaccine"), which protects against some strains of the [human papilloma virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_papilloma_virus "Human papilloma virus"), a contributing factor to some forms of [cervical cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cervical_cancer "Cervical cancer").[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Carney-135) Following the move, news outlets reported various apparent financial connections between Perry and the vaccine's manufacturer, [Merck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merck_&_Co. "Merck & Co.").[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Carney-135)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-136) Merck's [political action committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_action_committee "Political action committee") has contributed $28,500 since 2001 to Perry's campaigns.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-137) Perry later reversed his position, calling the vaccine mandate a "mistake".[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-RickPerryReversal-138) In May 2007, the Texas Legislature passed a bill undoing the order; Perry did not veto the bill, saying the veto would have been overruled, but blamed lawmakers who supported the bill for the deaths of future Texan cervical cancer victims.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-141)

On July 1, 2011, Perry both had adult [stem cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_cell "Stem cell") surgery in Houston and started "laying the groundwork" for the commercialization of the adult stem cell industry in Texas.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-TT-TXStemCellIndustry-142)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-NYT-PerryHasProcedure-143)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-144)

### Religion

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Rick_Perry_by_Gage_Skidmore_9.jpg/250px-Rick_Perry_by_Gage_Skidmore_9.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rick_Perry_by_Gage_Skidmore_9.jpg)Perry speaking at the 2014 [Conservative Political Action Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Political_Action_Conference "Conservative Political Action Conference") in Maryland

In 2006, Perry said he believed in the [inerrancy of the Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biblical_inerrancy "Biblical inerrancy") and that those who do not accept [Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus "Jesus") as their Savior will go to hell. A couple of days later, he clarified, "I don't know that there's any human being that has the ability to interpret what God and his final decision-making is going to be."[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-perryhagee-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-146)

In his 2008 book *On My Honor*, Perry expressed his views on the [Establishment Clause](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Establishment_Clause "Establishment Clause") and the [Free Exercise Clause](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Exercise_Clause "Free Exercise Clause") of the U.S. Constitution. "Let's be clear: I don't believe government, which taxes people regardless of their faith, should espouse a specific faith. I also don't think we should allow a small minority of [atheists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheist "Atheist") to sanitize our civil dialogue of religious references."[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-147)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-148)

In June 2011, Perry proclaimed August 6 as a Day of Prayer and [Fasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fasting "Fasting"), inviting other governors to join him in a prayer meeting hosted by the [American Family Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Family_Association "American Family Association") in Houston.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-149)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-150) The event was criticized as going beyond prayer and fasting to include launching Perry's presidential campaign.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-151)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-152)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-153)

Perry has called himself "a firm believer in [intelligent design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligent_design "Intelligent design") as a matter of faith and intellect" and has expressed support for its teaching alongside [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") in Texas schools but has also said that "educators and local school officials, not the governor, should determine science curriculum".[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-154)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-155)

### Education

In 2005, Perry said he would not "approve an education budget that shortchanges teacher salary increases, textbooks, education technology, and education reforms. And I cannot let $2 billion sit in some bank account when it can go directly to the classroom".[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-156)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-157)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-158)

Following a second rejection of Perry's bill, Perry asked [John Sharp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sharp_(Texas_politician) "John Sharp (Texas politician)") to head a task force charged with preparing a bipartisan education plan, which was subsequently adopted.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-CSHB2_Record_Vote-159)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-160)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-161)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-162)

In 2001, Perry expressed his pride in the enactment of the statute extending in-state tuition to [undocumented immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undocumented_immigrants "Undocumented immigrants") who meet Texas' residency requirements. It also required the undocumented students to pledge to apply for permanent residency or citizenship if this became a possibility for them.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-163) In September 2014, Gov. Perry stated during a debate his continuous support for the program.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-164)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-165)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-166)

### LGBT rights

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Rick_Perry_by_Gage_Skidmore_10.jpg/250px-Rick_Perry_by_Gage_Skidmore_10.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rick_Perry_by_Gage_Skidmore_10.jpg)Perry speaking at the 2015 [Conservative Political Action Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Political_Action_Conference "Conservative Political Action Conference") in National Harbor, Maryland

Perry opposed several LGBT rights measures, including legal recognition of same-sex relationships and openly gay military service, and drew criticism from LGBT rights organizations for his public comments and policy positions.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-167)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-168)

In 2002, Perry described the Texas same-sex [anti-sodomy law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodomy_law "Sodomy law") as "appropriate".[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-169) The following year, the [U.S. Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") struck down the statute in *[Lawrence v. Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_v._Texas "Lawrence v. Texas")*, determining that it violated the [Fourteenth Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution") to the Constitution.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-170)

In his 2010 book, Perry referenced the *Lawrence* decision, writing "Texans have a different view of the world than do the nine oligarchs in robes."[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Saenz-171) In 2011, Perry admitted that he did not know about the *Lawrence* decision; when told that the Supreme Court case had struck down Texas's anti-sodomy law, Perry said: "I'm not taking the [bar exam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_exam "Bar exam") [...] I don't know what a lot of legal cases [...] My position on traditional marriage is clear [...] I don't need a federal law case to explain it to me."[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Saenz-171)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-172)

Perry supported [Texas Proposition 2 in 2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Proposition_2_(2005) "Texas Proposition 2 (2005)"), a ballot proposition that [amended the Texas constitution by defining marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_former_U.S._state_constitutional_amendments_banning_same-sex_unions_by_type "List of former U.S. state constitutional amendments banning same-sex unions by type") as "only a union between a man and a woman" and prohibiting the state from creating or recognizing "any legal status identical or similar to marriage" (such as [civil unions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_union "Civil union")).[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-173)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-174)

In 2011, after [New York legalized same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage_Equality_Act_(New_York) "Marriage Equality Act (New York)"), Perry said it was their right to do so under the principle of [states' rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States'_rights "States' rights") in the [Tenth Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Tenth Amendment to the United States Constitution").[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-175) A spokesman later reiterated Perry's support for a [federal constitutional amendment banning same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Marriage_Amendment "Federal Marriage Amendment"), saying that position was not inconsistent, since an amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-176)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-177)

After the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in *[Obergefell v. Hodges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obergefell_v._Hodges "Obergefell v. Hodges")* in 2015 that the fundamental right to marry is guaranteed to same-sex couples by the Constitution, Perry condemned the decision, saying: "I'm a firm believer in traditional marriage, and I also believe the 10th Amendment leaves it to each state to decide this issue."[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-178)[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-179)

In his first book, *On My Honor*, published in 2008, Perry compared [homosexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality "Homosexuality") to [alcoholism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcoholism "Alcoholism"), writing that he is "no expert on the 'nature versus nurture' debate" but gays should simply choose abstinence.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-180) Perry's comments were criticized by LGBT rights groups.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-181)

During the 2012 presidential campaign, he criticized the repeal of the "[don't ask, don't tell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_ask,_don't_tell "Don't ask, don't tell")" policy for the U.S. military.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-182) In a 2011 campaign ad, he stated: "there's something wrong in this country when gays can serve openly in the military" and later defended the ad, saying he was "very comfortable" with it.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-183) Perry said using foreign aid as a policy tool against foreign countries that violate the human rights of homosexuals was "not in America's interests" and was part of a "war on traditional American values".[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-184)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-185)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-186)

Perry, an [Eagle Scout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagle_Scout_(Boy_Scouts_of_America) "Eagle Scout (Boy Scouts of America)"), called on the [Boy Scouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Scouts_of_America "Boy Scouts of America") in 2013 to continue their ban on homosexuality.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-187)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-188)

### Crime

Perry's campaigns for lieutenant governor and governor focused on a tough stance on crime. He has supported [block grants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_grant "Block grant") for crime programs.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-NGA10-189)

Jeff L. Blackburn, chief counsel of the [Innocence Project of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Innocence_Project_of_Texas "Innocence Project of Texas"), said of Perry that "He has done more good than any other governor we've ever had [...] unless, of course, it involves the death penalty. On the [death penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#Death_penalty), Rick Perry has a profound mental block."[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-NYTCrimeStance-190)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-191)

In 2001, Perry signed the James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Act, which strengthened penalties for crimes motivated by a person's race, color, disability, religion, national origin or ancestry, age, gender or sexual preference.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-192) The law was opposed by previous governor George Bush, who insisted that "all crimes are hate crimes."[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-193)[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-194)

In 2007, Perry signed a law ending automatic arrest for [cannabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis "Cannabis") possession.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-195)[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-196)

### Death penalty

Further information: [Capital punishment in Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment_in_Texas "Capital punishment in Texas")

Perry supports the [death penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_penalty "Death penalty").[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-197) In June 2001, he vetoed a ban on the [execution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_penalty "Death penalty") of [intellectually disabled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_disability "Intellectual disability") inmates.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-198) In 2011, during a televised debate for presidential candidates, he said he had "never struggled" with the question of the possible innocence of any of the 234 inmates executed to date while he was governor.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-199)[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-200)

Cases in which Perry has been criticized for his lack of intervention include those of [Cameron Todd Willingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Todd_Willingham "Cameron Todd Willingham") and Mexican nationals [José Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/José_Medellín "José Medellín") and [Humberto Leal Garcia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humberto_Leal_Garcia "Humberto Leal Garcia").[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-201)[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-grann1-202)[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-203)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-204)[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-205)[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-206)

Perry commuted the death sentence of [Kenneth Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Foster_(criminal) "Kenneth Foster (criminal)"), who was convicted of murder despite evidence that he was only present at the scene of the crime. Foster was convicted under a Texas law that makes co-conspirators liable in certain cases of homicide. In this case, it tied Foster to the triggerman. Perry raised doubts about the law and urged the legislature to re-examine the issue. "I believe the right and just decision is to commute Foster's sentence from the death penalty to life imprisonment," Perry said.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-207)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-208)

Perry also refused to grant a stay of execution in 2004 in the case of [Cameron Todd Willingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Todd_Willingham "Cameron Todd Willingham"), amid later questions about the reliability of the original arson investigation. The [Texas Forensic Science Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Forensic_Science_Commission "Texas Forensic Science Commission") subsequently examined the forensic evidence in the case. Perry said in 2009 that "Willingham was a monster. He was a guy who murdered his three children, who tried to beat his wife into an abortion so that he wouldn't have those kids. Person after person has stood up and testified to facts of this case that quite frankly you all aren't covering" and later replaced the chairman and other members of the Science Commission prior to a meeting on the case.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-209)[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-210) The replacements were believed to potentially related to the [election slated for the following year.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Texas_gubernatorial_election "2010 Texas gubernatorial election")[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-211)[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-212)[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-213)

### Infrastructure

In 2002, Perry proposed the [Trans-Texas Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans-Texas_Corridor "Trans-Texas Corridor") (TTC), a $175 billion transportation network that would include a 4,000-mile network of highways, rail, and utility lines and would be funded by private investors. Plans for the project were dropped in 2009 in favor of more incremental road projects.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-214)[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-215) Opposition to the project, also called the "[NAFTA super highway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAFTA_superhighway "NAFTA superhighway")" garnered opposition from rural Texans,[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-216) labor and environmentalists, the project became a major issue in the [2006 gubernatorial campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans-Texas_Corridor "Trans-Texas Corridor").[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-217)[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-218)

### Gun ownership

Perry has held a [Concealed Carry License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concealed_Carry_License "Concealed Carry License") (CCL)[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-219) and has signed a number of bills that increased CCL access.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-auto2-10)[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-220)

### Mexico border

In 2005, Perry launched Operation Linebacker, which was intended to prevent terrorists from exploiting the Texas-Mexico border. There was no evidence that terrorists attempted to exploit the border.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-texastribune-221)[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-222) Perry touted the border security efforts as he campaigned for re-election. During Perry's governorship, he launched additional operations and persuaded the Texas legislature to devote more taxpayers' resources to border security. According to a 2022 investigative report by the Texas Tribune, "The way the governors and their administrations have tracked success has fluctuated over the years, offering little clarity into whether the state is closer to securing the border today than it was nearly 20 years ago. Neither the governor's office nor the DPS, the main agency leading border security efforts, can provide a full breakdown of the state-led operations since 2005, their duration, their cost to taxpayers and their accomplishments."[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-texastribune-221)[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-223)[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-224)

During a large surge in [illegal immigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_immigration_to_the_United_States "Illegal immigration to the United States") through the U.S. southern border in the summer of 2014, Perry criticized U.S. President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"), saying the surge was "a humanitarian crisis that he has the ability to stop".[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-225) On July 21, 2014, Perry announced he would send in 1,000 [National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Guard_of_the_United_States "National Guard of the United States") troops to secure the border.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-226)[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-227) Although illegal immigration levels declined over 70% after Perry deployed the National Guard, [PolitiFact.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PolitiFact.com "PolitiFact.com") rated his claim that the decline resulted from the surge as "mostly false".[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-228)[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-229)[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-230)

In 2016, *The Texas Tribune* wrote that "Perry has long been a critic of building a wall or fence along the border."[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-231) After Trump won the Republican presidential nomination in 2016, Perry fully embraced Trump's proposed border wall.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-232)[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-233)

### Veto controversy and exoneration

Main article: [Rick Perry veto controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry_veto_controversy "Rick Perry veto controversy")

On August 15, 2014, Perry was [indicted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indictment#United_States "Indictment") by a Travis County [grand jury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_jury "Grand jury").[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-234) The first charge of the [indictment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indictment "Indictment") was abuse of official capacity, which has since been ruled unconstitutional,[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-MalewitzTXTrib02242016-235) for threatening to veto $7.5 million in funding for the Public Integrity Unit, a state public corruption prosecutors department. The second charge, which has also since been ruled unconstitutional, was coercion of a public servant, for seeking the resignation of Travis County District Attorney [Rosemary Lehmberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary_Lehmberg "Rosemary Lehmberg"), a Democrat, after she was convicted of [drunk driving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drunk_driving "Drunk driving") and incarcerated.[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-MalewitzTXTrib02242016-235)[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-FOXNews140815-236)[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-NYTimes.Gov-237)[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-238)[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-239)

Perry pleaded not guilty to both charges. Perry's supporters called the charges political and partisan,[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-LATimes140815-240) and several Democratic commentators, including [David Axelrod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Axelrod "David Axelrod"), believed charges were weak.[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-WaPo120815-241)[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-BizInside08162014-242)[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-243)

In February 2016, Perry was cleared of all charges.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-244)[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-245)[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-246)

The [Texas Court of Criminal Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Court_of_Criminal_Appeals "Texas Court of Criminal Appeals") ruled that courts could not limit [veto power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veto_power "Veto power") and that prosecuting Perry over his action violates "the [separation of powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Separation_of_powers "Separation of powers") provision of the Texas Constitution" and infringed on Perry's [First Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "First Amendment to the United States Constitution") right to [freedom of speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_speech "Freedom of speech").[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-MalewitzTXTrib02242016-235)[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-247)[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-248)

### Retirement as governor

See also: [Political positions of Rick Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_positions_of_Rick_Perry "Political positions of Rick Perry") and [2016 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election")

By the end of his third full term, he had served more than 14 consecutive years in office. A University of Texas at Austin–*[Texas Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Tribune "Texas Tribune")* poll released in June 2013, showed Perry leading potential primary challenger Attorney General [Greg Abbott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Abbott "Greg Abbott") by double digits, 45–19%.[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-249) In February, the same poll had Perry leading by a 3-to-1 margin (49–17%) of 32 points over Abbott.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-250)[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-251)

However, Perry decided not to run for re-election to a fourth full term, announcing in front of family and supporters at the [Holt Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holt_Manufacturing_Company "Holt Manufacturing Company") headquarters in [San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio "San Antonio") on July 8, 2013, that he would retire instead.[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-abclocal1-252)[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-253)[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-254)

Perry retired with the 10th longest gubernatorial tenure in United States history at the end of his term on January 20, 2015, at 5,143 days as well as the record of the longest serving Texas governor.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-255)[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-256)[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-257)[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-258)

## Presidential campaigns

### 2012

Main article: [Rick Perry 2012 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry_2012_presidential_campaign "Rick Perry 2012 presidential campaign")

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/RickPerry_Iowa_Fair_b.jpg/250px-RickPerry_Iowa_Fair_b.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RickPerry_Iowa_Fair_b.jpg)Perry campaigning at the [Iowa State Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_State_Fair "Iowa State Fair"), August 14, 2011

Perry was considered as a potential candidate since as early as the [2008 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election "2008 United States presidential election"), initially denying he was interested in the office but later becoming more open-minded. He formally launched his campaign on August 13, 2011, in [Charleston, South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston,_South_Carolina "Charleston, South Carolina").[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-nyt110813-259)[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-260)

Perry was initially successful in fundraising and was briefly considered a serious contender for the nomination.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-reu120104-261)[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-lat120103-262) However, Perry's performances in the GOP debates received generally poor reviews from the media. His botched attempt to criticize [Mitt Romney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney "Mitt Romney") as a [flip-flopper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip-flop_(politics) "Flip-flop (politics)") in a debate held in [Orlando, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida") was criticized in news coverage.[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-263) Perry lost many conservatives' support when he defended the Texas policy of allowing in-state tuition for the children of illegal immigrants. He said during one debate that those who opposed financially supporting their education didn't "have a heart."[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-264) After he mishandled a question about how he would respond to a "3am call" as president, Perry's advisers insisted that he get more sleep before the remaining debates.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-265)[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-266)[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-267)[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-268)[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-269)

At the November 9, 2011 Republican debate, Perry began a fiery statement about his platform, pledging to eliminate three government agencies as part of his policy to cut federal spending. After naming the [Departments of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Education "United States Department of Education") and the [Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Commerce "United States Department of Commerce"), he was unable to remember the name of the third agency, eventually declaring "I can't. The third one, I can't. Sorry. Oops."[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-270) A few minutes later, Perry said that the third agency he proposed to eliminate was the [Department of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Energy "United States Department of Energy") (he would later become the [Secretary of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Secretary of Energy") under the Trump administration).[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-271) *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* called it "one of the most humiliating debate performances in recent US political history".[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-272)[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-273)[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-274)[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-275)

After finishing fifth with just over 10% of the vote in the [Iowa caucuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_caucuses "Iowa caucuses") on January 3, 2012, Perry considered dropping out of the presidential race but did not.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-reu120104-261)[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-lat120103-262) After a poor showing in New Hampshire and with "lagging" poll numbers in South Carolina, Perry formally announced he was suspending his campaign on January 19, 2012.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-nyt120119a-11) CNN later stated that Perry's 2012 campaign "was crushed by the weight of his debate gaffe and stump speech mishaps".[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-cnn._Rick-276)[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-277)[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-278)

### 2016

Main article: [Rick Perry 2016 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry_2016_presidential_campaign "Rick Perry 2016 presidential campaign")

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ab/Former_Texas_Governor_Rick_Perry_speaking_at_2015_FITN_%28First_in_the_Nation%29_Republican_Leadership_Summit_in_New_Hampshire.jpg/250px-Former_Texas_Governor_Rick_Perry_speaking_at_2015_FITN_%28First_in_the_Nation%29_Republican_Leadership_Summit_in_New_Hampshire.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Former_Texas_Governor_Rick_Perry_speaking_at_2015_FITN_(First_in_the_Nation)_Republican_Leadership_Summit_in_New_Hampshire.jpg)Perry speaking at 2015 First in the Nation Republican Leadership Summit in [New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire "New Hampshire")

Almost immediately following the 2012 election, Perry was mentioned as a potential candidate for the presidency in the 2016 presidential election. A July 2013 *[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")* magazine article stated that "everything is aligned for Rick Perry to be the Republican nominee for president in 2016."[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-279)[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-280)

Perry officially launched his 2016 presidential candidacy on June 4, 2015, in [Addison, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addison,_Texas "Addison, Texas").[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-cnn._Rick-276)[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-281)

Perry withdrew his candidacy on September 11, 2015, following poor polling after the first debate. He became the first in the field of major candidates to drop out of the race.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-auto1-15) In the weeks before he dropped out of the race, Perry's campaign was in dire straits financially, having spent nearly four times as much as was raised.[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-282)[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-283)[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-284)

On January 25, 2016, Perry endorsed United States Senator [Ted Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz "Ted Cruz") (R-TX) for president.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-285) On May 5, 2016, following the suspension of Cruz's presidential campaign, Perry endorsed Donald Trump for the presidency.[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-286)[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-287)[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-288)

## Secretary of Energy
