[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/31/Secretary_Rick_Perry_at_2017_Energy_Project_Management_Awards.jpg/250px-Secretary_Rick_Perry_at_2017_Energy_Project_Management_Awards.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Rick_Perry_at_2017_Energy_Project_Management_Awards.jpg)Perry at the 2017 Energy Project Management Awards on March 22, 2017[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Senator_Joe_Manchin%2C_Secreatry_Perry%2C_Senator_Shelley_Moore_Capito%2C_and_U.S._Rep._David_McKinley_at_NETL_%2834999869724%29.jpg/250px-Senator_Joe_Manchin%2C_Secreatry_Perry%2C_Senator_Shelley_Moore_Capito%2C_and_U.S._Rep._David_McKinley_at_NETL_%2834999869724%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Senator_Joe_Manchin,_Secreatry_Perry,_Senator_Shelley_Moore_Capito,_and_U.S._Rep._David_McKinley_at_NETL_(34999869724).jpg)Perry with [Joe Manchin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manchin "Joe Manchin"), [Shelley Moore Capito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelley_Moore_Capito "Shelley Moore Capito"), and [David McKinley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_McKinley "David McKinley") in 2017

On December 14, 2016, President-elect Trump nominated Perry as Secretary of Energy.[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-289) The nomination initially faced heavy criticism as [Perry had called for the Department of Energy to be abolished during his 2012 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Republican_Party_presidential_debates_and_forums#November_9,_2011_–_Auburn_Hills,_Michigan "2012 Republican Party presidential debates and forums")[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-290) and had been unable to remember the name of the department during a presidential debate.[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-291) His nomination was approved by a 16–7 vote from the [United States Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Energy_and_Natural_Resources "United States Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources") on January 31, 2017.[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-292)[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-293)[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-294)

On March 2, 2017, the United States Senate voted 62–37 to confirm Perry.[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-295) The next month, Perry ordered a study of the [U.S. electric grid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_U.S._power_transmission_grid "Continental U.S. power transmission grid") with particular consideration to [coal power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coal_power_in_the_United_States "Coal power in the United States").[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-296)[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-297) In January 2018, the [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Energy_Regulatory_Commission "Federal Energy Regulatory Commission") unanimously rejected a proposal backed by Perry to subsidize coal and nuclear power plants that stored fuel on-site.[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-298)[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-299)

In a CNBC interview on June 19, 2017, when asked about the role of human activity in the recent rise of the Earth's temperature, Perry said, "The fact is this shouldn't be a debate about, 'Is the climate changing, is man having an effect on it?' Yeah, we are. The question should be just how much, and what are the policy changes that we need to make to effect that?"[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-300)[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-301)

In July 2017, Perry strongly expressed his support for Donald Trump's ban on transgender people from serving in the U.S. military stating that "The idea that the American people need to be paying for these types of operations to change your sex is not very wise from a standpoint of economics."[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-302)[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-303)

In November 2017, Perry suggested that using fossil fuels to light dangerous places in Africa could reduce sexual assault, saying, "When the lights are on, when you have light that shines the righteousness, if you will, on those types of acts." Perry was criticized by the [Sierra Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Club "Sierra Club") for "exploiting the struggle of those most affected by climate change".[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-304)[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-305)[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-306)

For one week in November 2018, it was reported that the U.S. had become a net exporter of oil, temporarily ending nearly 75 continuous years of dependence on foreign oil.[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-307)[[308]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-308)

On October 4, 2019, the *New York Times* reported that he was expected to resign as Secretary of Energy by the end of 2019, based on information from anonymous sources.[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-309) On October 17, 2019, Perry told Trump he would resign by the end of the year, ultimately departing at the beginning of December.[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-310)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-HillLastDay-17)[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-311)

### Trump–Ukraine scandal

Main article: [Trump–Ukraine scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump–Ukraine_scandal "Trump–Ukraine scandal")

A little more than a month after Perry attended Zelenskyy's May 2019 inauguration, Ukraine awarded the contract to Perry's supporters after Perry recommended one of them to be Zelenskyy's energy adviser. The recommendation was made as Zelenskyy was attempting to secure the nearly $400 million in U.S. military aid. A week after Perry attended the inauguration, "Ukrainian Energy", a new joint venture between Michael Bleyzer's investment firm SigmaBleyzer and Alex Cranberg's Aspect Energy, submitted a bid for a 50-year drilling contract at a Ukraine government-controlled site called Varvynska.[[312]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-BleyzerCranbergPerry-312)[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-313)[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-314)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Volodymyr_Zelensky_2019_presidential_inauguration_45_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Volodymyr_Zelensky_2019_presidential_inauguration_45_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Volodymyr_Zelensky_2019_presidential_inauguration_45_(cropped).jpg)Perry and Zelenskyy at Zelenskyy's May 2019 inauguration

A [July 25, 2019 telephone call](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_investigations_into_Trump_and_Russia_(2019)#20190725 "Timeline of investigations into Trump and Russia (2019)") between Trump and [Ukrainian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") president [Volodymyr Zelenskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Volodymyr Zelenskyy") led in September to [a whistleblower complaint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump–Ukraine_scandal "Trump–Ukraine scandal") and an [impeachment inquiry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_inquiry_against_Donald_Trump "Impeachment inquiry against Donald Trump") against Trump. Two weeks after the inquiry was launched, Trump claimed in a conference call with Congressional Republican leaders that he had only made the telephone call at Perry's urging.[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-315) Perry's spokesperson said that Perry had suggested Trump discuss energy security with Zelenskyy, but energy was not mentioned in the publicly released memo about the conversations, which instead focused on Trump asking Zelenskyy to launch investigations into [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden"), [Hunter Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_Biden "Hunter Biden"), [Crowdstrike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdstrike "Crowdstrike"), and the [2016 U.S. presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_U.S._presidential_election "2016 U.S. presidential election").[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-316) Per Trump's direction earlier that year, Perry spoke with [Rudy Giuliani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy_Giuliani "Rudy Giuliani") about Ukraine, which [Mick Mulvaney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Mulvaney "Mick Mulvaney") confirmed.[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-317)[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-318)[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-319) Perry denied ever mentioning the Bidens in his discussions with Trump or Ukrainian officials.[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-320) Mulvaney had put [Gordon Sondland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Sondland "Gordon Sondland"), [Kurt Volker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Volker "Kurt Volker"), and Perry in charge of managing the [Ukraine–United States relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine–United_States_relations "Ukraine–United States relations") instead of diplomats at the [National Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Security_Council "United States National Security Council") and the [US Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Department_of_State "US Department of State").[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-321)[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-322)[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-323)[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-324)

Perry was mentioned in October 2019 by former U.S. officials in relation to reports he planned to have [Amos Hochstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amos_Hochstein "Amos Hochstein") replaced as a member of the board at [Naftogaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naftogaz "Naftogaz") with someone aligned with Republican interests. Perry denied the reports.[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-325)[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-326) In November 2019, both Sondland and [David Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Holmes_(diplomat) "David Holmes (diplomat)"), who serves as counselor of political affairs at the U.S. Embassy in Ukraine, testified that Perry had played a senior role in the Ukraine campaign, with Holmes even describing Perry, along with Sondland and Volker, was one of the "Three Amigos" who directly assisted both Trump and Giuliani.[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-327)[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-328)[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-329)[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-330)[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-331)[[332]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-332)[[333]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-333)

## Career outside politics

In February 2015, Perry announced that he would join the board of directors of [Energy Transfer Partners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_Transfer_Partners "Energy Transfer Partners"),[[334]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-etp_bio-334) which owns and operates one of the largest energy asset portfolios in the United States, and Sunoco Partners, another major Dallas energy company.[[335]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-etp_about-335)[[336]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Dallas_News-336) According to SEC filings, Perry resigned from the boards of both companies on December 31, 2016.[[336]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Dallas_News-336) In early January 2020, Perry joined the board of LE GP, general partner of Energy Transfer.[[337]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-337)[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-338) In February 2020, Perry rejoined MCNA Dental's board of directors as chief strategy officer and vice chairman.[[339]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-339)[[340]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-340)[[341]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-341)[[342]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-342)

On October 1, 2025, Perry, along with his son Griffin and conservative donor and investor [Toby Neugebauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toby_Neugebauer "Toby Neugebauer"), launched Fermi America, a data center real estate investment trust, which planned to expand into nuclear energy.[[343]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-343)[[344]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-344) The company planned to build an 11-gigawatt energy and data center campus on a 5,236-acre site (2,119 ha) located outside [Amarillo, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarillo,_Texas "Amarillo, Texas"). In paperwork filed with regulators, the site is to be named the “Donald J. Trump Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus”.[[345]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-345) Although the company had no announced customers, construction, or revenue, the [IPO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPO "IPO") in October gave the company a market cap of $16 billion, with Perry's stake worth roughly $500 million.[[346]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-346)[[347]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-347) In 2019, Forbes had estimated Perry's net worth at $3 million. By April 2026, Fermi had not secured a major data-center tenant, and its shares had fallen substantially from their initial offering price. The company also announced a change in its executive leadership.[[348]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-348)[[349]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-349)

### Ibogaine advocacy

Since consuming [ibogaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibogaine "Ibogaine") at a clinic in Mexico in September 2023, Perry has become an outspoken advocate for the drug and [psychedelic-assisted therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychedelic-assisted_therapy "Psychedelic-assisted therapy"), describing his public activities surrounding ibogaine as "[his] life's mission". To this end, he supported legislative efforts in Texas to fund clinical trials for treating military veterans with ibogaine, co-founded a non-profit organization that is focused on advancing ibogaine therapy in the United States, and has spoken publicly about his experiences with the drug.[[354]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Draper2025-354) In 2025, Texas enacted legislation supporting a state-funded ibogaine clinical research program; the state allocated $50 million toward the trials. In March 2026, Texas officials announced that the program would proceed without the originally envisioned private drug-company partner.[[355]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-355)[[356]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-356)[[357]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-357)[[358]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-358)[[359]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-359)

## Personal life

Perry grew up in the [United Methodist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Methodist_Church "United Methodist Church"). He and his family were members of Tarrytown United Methodist Church in Austin until 2010, when they began attending Lake Hills Church, a non-denominational [evangelical Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical_Christian "Evangelical Christian") [megachurch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megachurch "Megachurch") in western Travis County.[[360]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-christianpost.com-360) Perry told the *Austin American-Statesman* that he began attending Lake Hills because it was close to the rental home where he and his wife lived while the governor's mansion was being renovated.[[361]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Statesman-361) He was baptized in 2014.[[360]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-christianpost.com-360)[[362]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-362)[[363]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-363)

In 1982, Perry married [Mary Anita Thigpen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Thigpen_Perry "Anita Thigpen Perry"), his childhood sweetheart whom he had known since [elementary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_school "Elementary school"). They have two adult children, Griffin and Sydney. Anita attended [West Texas State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Texas_State_University "West Texas State University") and earned a degree in nursing. She has spearheaded a number of health-related initiatives such as the Anita Thigpen Perry Endowment at the [University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_Health_Science_Center_at_San_Antonio "University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio"), which focuses on nutrition, [cardiovascular disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiovascular_disease "Cardiovascular disease"), [health education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_education "Health education"), and early childhood development.[[364]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-364) She helped develop and host the [Texas Conference for Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Conference_for_Women "Texas Conference for Women").[[365]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Texas_Conference_for_Women-365)[[366]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-366)[[367]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-367)

Perry played himself in minor roles for several feature films, including *[Man of the House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_of_the_House_(2005_film) "Man of the House (2005 film)")*, *Deep in the Heart*, and *[Hating Breitbart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hating_Breitbart "Hating Breitbart")*.[[368]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-368)[[369]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-369)

Perry is a member of the National Society of the [Sons of the American Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sons_of_the_American_Revolution "Sons of the American Revolution") and was awarded its Gold Good Citizenship Medal.[[370]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-370)[[371]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-371)[[372]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-372)

Perry has described his personal experiences with [ibogaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibogaine "Ibogaine") and [5-MeO-DMT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5-MeO-DMT "5-MeO-DMT") in [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico") in 2023.[[354]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Draper2025-354)[[373]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-Lhooq2026-373)[[374]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry#cite_note-374)

**Danny Ray Brouillette**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-1) ([/bruːˈjɛt/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") born August 18, 1962) is an American government official, lobbyist, businessman, and [Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Army "US Army") veteran who served as the 15th [United States Secretary of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Secretary of Energy") in the [first Donald Trump administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "First presidency of Donald Trump") from 2019 to 2021.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-2) He previously served as the [United States Deputy Secretary of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Deputy Secretary of Energy") from August 2017 to December 2019. In 2023, Brouillette was named president and chief executive officer elect of the [Edison Electric Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edison_Electric_Institute "Edison Electric Institute").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-3)

## Early life and career

Danny Ray Brouillette was born on August 18, 1962, in [Paincourtville, Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paincourtville,_Louisiana "Paincourtville, Louisiana"). He graduated from the [University of Maryland Global Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maryland_Global_Campus "University of Maryland Global Campus") in 1995.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:1-4)

Following his service in the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army"), Brouillette was U.S. representative [Billy Tauzin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Tauzin "Billy Tauzin")'s legislative director from 1989 to 1997.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:1-4) From 1997 to 2000, he was Senior Vice President of R. Duffy Wall & Associates,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-5) a DC-based lobbying firm.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-6) Brouillette was Assistant Secretary for Congressional and Intergovernmental Affairs in the [United States Department of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Energy "United States Department of Energy") from 2001 to 2003 under President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:0-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-8)

He was chief of staff under Rep. Billy Tauzin and was also staff director for the [United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Energy_and_Commerce "United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce") from 2003 to 2004, when Tauzin chaired the committee.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:2-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:3-10) Brouillette was involved in crafting provisions included in the [Energy Policy Act of 2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_Policy_Act_of_2005 "Energy Policy Act of 2005"), specifically with respect to the Department of Energy loan guarantee program and federal authorization of importation and exportation of liquid natural gas.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:2-9)

From 2004 to 2006, Brouillette was a vice president at [Ford Motor Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company "Ford Motor Company") and sat on Ford's North American Operating Committee.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:2-9) In 2006, Brouillette became head of public policy and senior vice president at [United Services Automobile Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USAA "USAA").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-11)

Brouillette was a member of Louisiana's State Mineral and Energy Board from 2013 to 2016.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:3-10) He was awarded the 2020 Distinguished Alumnus Award by the [University of Maryland Global Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maryland_Global_Campus "University of Maryland Global Campus") [Alumni Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alumni_association "Alumni association").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-12) In 2021, he joined the [American Council for Capital Formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Council_for_Capital_Formation "American Council for Capital Formation")'s board of advisors.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-14)

### Deputy Secretary of Energy (2017–2019)

On April 3, 2017, President Donald Trump announced he would nominate Brouillette as [United States Deputy Secretary of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Deputy Secretary of Energy") in the United States Department of Energy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:0-7) Brouillette was confirmed by the U.S. Senate on August 3, 2017. He was sworn in as the Deputy Secretary of Energy on August 8, 2017.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-15)

### Secretary of Energy (2019–2021)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Dan_Brouillette_sworn_in_as_Secretary_of_Energy.jpg/250px-Dan_Brouillette_sworn_in_as_Secretary_of_Energy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dan_Brouillette_sworn_in_as_Secretary_of_Energy.jpg)Dan Brouillette being sworn in on December 11, 2019.

On October 18, 2019, President Trump announced he would nominate Brouillette as [United States Secretary of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Secretary of Energy") to replace [Rick Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry "Rick Perry"), who had announced he would step down by the end of the year.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-trumptweetnom-16) On November 7, 2019, President Trump sent his nomination to the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-17)

Perry formally resigned as Energy Secretary on December 1, 2019, making Brouillette the acting secretary, as his nomination was still pending before the U.S. Senate. On December 2, 2019, the Senate confirmed his nomination by a vote of 70–15.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-18) Brouillette was formally sworn in on December 11, 2019.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-19) Then-Under Secretary of Energy [Mark Menezes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Menezes "Mark Menezes") served as Acting Deputy Secretary of Energy until he was confirmed as Deputy Secretary on August 4, 2020.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-20)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Secretary_Dan_Brouillette.jpg/250px-Secretary_Dan_Brouillette.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Dan_Brouillette.jpg)Secretary Brouillette speaks at a farewell event at the Department of Energy Headquarters in [Washington D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") in January 2021.

In December 2020, as part of the recently signed [Abraham Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Accords "Abraham Accords"), Brouillette convened a "first-of-its kind" meeting between the energy minister of Israel and counterparts from several Arab nations.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-21)

On January 7, 2021, Brouillette promised a seamless handover between the [Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "First presidency of Donald Trump") and [Biden administrations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biden_administration "Biden administration").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-22)

## Post-Trump administration

### Sempra Infrastructure

Brouillette was named the president of [Sempra Infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sempra "Sempra") in July 2021 and started with the company in November of that year.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-23) During his time with Sempra, Brouillette oversaw the Port Arthur [LNG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquefied_natural_gas "Liquefied natural gas") project in Texas[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-24) and a heads of agreement deal with TotalEnergies, Mitsui, Mitsubishi and NYK for Cameron LNG Phase 2.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-25)

### Edison Electric Institute

On August 16, 2023, the [Edison Electric Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edison_Electric_Institute "Edison Electric Institute"), the [interest group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advocacy_group "Advocacy group") for United States [investor-owned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investor-owned_utilities_in_the_United_States "Investor-owned utilities in the United States") [electric utilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_utility "Electric utility"), named Brouillette its president and chief executive officer, effective January 1, 2024.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-26) He resigned on October 28, 2024, less than 10 months after taking the position, saying he wanted to focus on global energy issues.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-27)

## Personal life

Brouillette and his wife, Adrienne, are U.S. Army veterans and the parents of nine children, all of whom the couple homeschooled.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-28) They reside in [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Brouillette#cite_note-:0-7) He served in the Army from 1982 to 1987 as a tank commander in Germany in the "[Fulda Gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulda_Gap "Fulda Gap")" and as a [Drill Sergeant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drill_instructor#United_States "Drill instructor") in the [Army Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Reserve "United States Army Reserve") in South Carolina.

**David G. Huizenga** is an American civil servant who serves as the associate principal deputy administrator of the [National Nuclear Security Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Nuclear_Security_Administration "National Nuclear Security Administration"), and was the acting [United States secretary of energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Secretary of Energy").

## Education

Huizenga attended [Montana State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana_State_University "Montana State University"), graduating with a bachelor's degree in chemistry, followed by a master's degree in chemical engineering.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Huizenga#cite_note-1)

## Acting Secretary of Energy

On January 20, 2021 following the [inauguration of President Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inauguration_of_Joe_Biden "Inauguration of Joe Biden"), Huizenga was selected to act as acting United States Secretary of Energy, pending the confirmation of nominee [Jennifer Granholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Granholm "Jennifer Granholm") by the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Huizenga#cite_note-2)
